extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent practitioners and patent examiners (applicants, patent attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the use, scope, and sufficiency of affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131(a) to antedate prior art and overcome pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102/103 rejections, including when such affidavits are appropriate or inappropriate and what proof is required (conception, reduction to practice, diligence, derivation, coauthorship, genus/species rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of printed publications and patents as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Any printed publication or activity dated prior to the effective filing date of applicant's or patent owner's claimed invention, or any domestic patent of prior filing date, which in its disclosure is pertinent to the claimed invention, is available for use by the examiner as a reference in the rejection of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent application publications and certain international application publications having an effective prior art date prior to the effective filing date may be used in a rejection. See MPEP §§ 2136 - 2136.03 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of a 37 CFR 1.131(a) affidavit or declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of a 37 CFR 1.131(a) affidavit or declaration is to overcome a prior art rejection under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103 by proving invention of the claimed subject matter by the inventor or at least one joint inventor prior to the effective date of the reference or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Swearing behind withdraws the rejection (not the reference). Alternative remedies (e.g., 1.132 affidavits) may be available in some situations; see related MPEP sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible situations for using 37 CFR 1.131(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 may be used to overcome rejections in applications subject to pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 and to overcome rejections under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) in certain situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: (A) to antedate a reference qualifying under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a) when the reference date is less than one year prior to the effective filing date (but not if the reference claims interfering subject matter per 37 CFR 41.203(a)); (B) to antedate references qualifying under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) where the reference has an earlier effective date and shows but does not claim interfering subject matter; (C) during examination, to antedate an activity that qualifies under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) and not under 102(b). See MPEP § 715 for full context.

rubrics_metrics.name: When 37 CFR 1.131(a) affidavits are inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(a) is not appropriate in specified situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific inapplicable situations include: (A) application subject to current 35 U.S.C. 102 and affidavit not directed to pre‑AIA 102(g) evidence; (B) reference publication date is more than 1 year prior to effective filing date (statutory bar under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)); (C) reference U.S. patent or application publication claims interfering subject matter (see 37 CFR 41.203(a)); (D) foreign patent for same invention issued before domestic filing where foreign application was filed >12 months earlier (pre‑AIA 102(d)); (E) applicant's effective filing date is prior to the reference's effective date (affidavit unnecessary); (F) reference claims same invention and claimed invention under examination is subject to statutory double patenting; (G) applicant has clearly admitted on the record that the subject matter is prior art; (H) subject matter relied upon is prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f); (I) subject matter corresponding to a lost count in an interference may be unavailable or barred by interference estoppel (see cited cases and MPEP guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of a reference to be overcome
rubrics_metrics.description: The date to be overcome under 37 CFR 1.131(a) is the effective date of the reference (i.e., the date on which the reference is available as prior art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a domestic patent used as a reference under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e), the effective date is the earlier of the actual filing date of the reference U.S. patent or U.S. patent application and the earliest claimed domestic benefit date that the reference is entitled to — not the foreign priority date. See MPEP §§ 2136 - 2136.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of activities to be overcome
rubrics_metrics.description: For activities, the effective date to be overcome is the date the activity was first known to have occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant admissions, submitted evidence of use or knowledge by others, or examiner's personal knowledge may establish the activity date. See MPEP §§ 2120.02 and 2133.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph: Ineffective — Reference is a statutory bar
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.60.fti: The reference is a statutory bar under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) and thus cannot be overcome by an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this when the reference is >1 year before effective filing date or otherwise a statutory bar. Follow with appropriate explanatory paragraphs (7.58.fti–7.63.fti) or set forth proper basis for insufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient evidence of reduction to practice before reference date
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavit/declaration is ineffective if evidence is insufficient to establish a reduction to practice of the invention in this country or a NAFTA/WTO member country prior to the effective date of the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.59.fti (must be preceded by 7.57.fti). Examiner should state deficiencies; reduction to practice must be in this country or NAFTA/WTO member country for 1.131(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient evidence of conception
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavit/declaration is ineffective if evidence is insufficient to establish conception of the invention prior to the effective date of the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conception is the mental part of the inventive act but must be capable of proof (demonstrative evidence or a complete disclosure to another). Conception is more than a vague idea; the requisite means and their interaction must be comprehended. See form paragraph 7.61.fti and cited case law (Mergenthaler v. Scudder). If affidavit also fails to establish diligence or reduction to practice, follow with form paragraphs 7.62.fti and/or 7.63.fti.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence requirement and lack of diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavit/declaration must establish diligence from a date prior to the date of reduction to practice of the reference to either a constructive reduction to practice or an actual reduction to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If evidence is insufficient to establish such diligence, use form paragraph 7.62.fti. Diligence is not required after reduction to practice. If conception not shown, 7.61.fti must precede 7.62.fti. Provide explanation for non‑diligence in examiner bracket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient evidence of actual reduction to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavit/declaration is ineffective if evidence is insufficient to establish an alleged actual reduction to practice of the invention in this country or a NAFTA/WTO member country after the effective date of the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.63.fti (preceded by 7.57.fti). If alleged reduction to practice actually predates the reference, do not use this paragraph (use 7.59.fti instead). Provide explanation of lack of showing in bracket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit/declaration effective to overcome reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.64.fti: The affidavit or declaration filed on [date] under 37 CFR 1.131(a) is sufficient to overcome the [reference].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert appropriate dates/names in form. Use when the 1.131(a) evidence meets the requirements discussed (possession, conception, reduction to practice or commensurate showing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency when reference names different inventive entity (use of 1.131 vs 1.132)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reference names an inventive entity including joint inventor S and another joint inventor, and a later application names sole inventor S, the reference may be applied until overcome by an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(a) showing prior invention or by an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.132 traversing the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unequivocal 1.132 declaration by S that S conceived or invented the subject matter disclosed but not claimed in the reference has been sufficient in some cases. However, a naked assertion of inventorship without context/explanation/evidence is insufficient (EmeraChem v. Volkswagen). If the reference includes claims reciting the relied‑upon subject matter, a 1.132 declaration must also explain the presence of the additional joint inventor. Testimony from other joint inventors is usually not required but may be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common assignee does not substitute for 1.131 showing
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere fact that the reference and the application under examination are owned by the same assignee does not avoid the necessity of filing an affidavit under 37 CFR 1.131(a) in the absence of a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that the patentee derived the subject matter from the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common ownership does not grant rights beyond what would exist otherwise. However, in some rejections (e.g., pre‑AIA 102(f)/(g) or 102(e)/103 pairings), a showing that the invention was commonly owned or subject to obligation to assign at the time may preclude the rejection; see MPEP §§ 2146.01–2146.02 and § 2154.02(c) for AIA applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of inventor's own invention can be overcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless it is a statutory bar, a rejection under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 based on a publication may be overcome by showing that it was published either by the inventor, at least one joint inventor, or on behalf of the inventor or at least one joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because such a showing is not made to show a date of invention under 37 CFR 1.131(a), the limitation that only acts in this country or NAFTA/WTO member countries may be relied on to establish a date of invention is not applicable for this showing. Use 1.132 affidavits for such purposes; see MPEP § 716.10 and §§ 2153–2154 for AIA context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co‑authorship: when a coauthor is inventor/joint inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the inventor or at least one joint inventor is a co‑author of a publication cited against an application, a rejection under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (e) based on the publication may be overcome by filing an affidavit or declaration of the inventor/joint inventor under 37 CFR 1.131(a) or a specific 1.132 affidavit showing the publication describes the work of the inventor/joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An uncorroborated affidavit by a sole inventor indicating sole inventorship has been sufficient in some cases (In re Katz). But a naked assertion without context/explanation/evidence is insufficient (EmeraChem). Corroboration or supporting context is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation: evidence required when reference disclosure derived from inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: When the unclaimed subject matter of a patent, application publication, or other publication is the inventor’s or at least one joint inventor’s own invention, the inventor must submit evidence establishing that the patentee/applicant/author derived their knowledge of the relevant subject matter from the inventor and that the inventor made the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derivation in pre‑AIA law requires showing both derivation of knowledge and that the inventor made the invention. See In re Mathews and In re Facius and MPEP §§ 2132.01, 2136.05 and 2137.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities applied against claims may be antedated
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless it is a statutory bar, a rejection under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103 based on an activity showing use or knowledge prior to filing may be overcome by a 37 CFR 1.131(a) affidavit establishing a date of invention prior to the activity, or by a 1.132 affidavit showing the activity was performed by the inventor or a joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 715.01(d) for context. The activity's effective date is when it was first known to have occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: How much of the claimed invention must be shown (possession requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 37 CFR 1.131(a) affidavit or declaration must establish possession of either the whole invention claimed or something falling within the claim (such as a species of a claimed genus), in the sense that the claim as a whole reads on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An affidavit that shows only part of the claimed invention (e.g., missing an element) is generally insufficient (In re Tanczyn). However, if differences are so small as to render the claims obvious over the reference(s), the affidavit need only show no more than the reference shows (In re Stryker). The affidavit must still establish possession of the basic inventive concept and not merely what a reference shows (In re Spiller).

rubrics_metrics.name: Swearing behind one of multiple combined references
rubrics_metrics.description: To overcome a pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) rejection based on a combination of references, applicant may show completion of the invention prior to the effective date of any of the references; applicant need not antedate the reference with the earliest prior art date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when relying on antedating a later reference, the 1.131(a) affidavit must still establish possession of the claimed invention (basic inventive concept), not merely of what one reference shows if that reference does not teach the inventive concept. Examiner may consider teachings of the other reference(s) to show differences would have been obvious prior to the earlier reference date.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule as to generic claims (species antedating genus)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference or activity applied against generic claims may (in most cases) be antedated as to such claims by a 37 CFR 1.131(a) affidavit showing completion of the invention of only a single species within the genus before the prior art date of the reference or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precedents (Ex parte Biesecker; In re Fong; In re Dafano) support this, but practice differs for cases in unpredictable arts — see MPEP § 715.03 for guidance relative to predictability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice relative to cases where predictability is in question (genus‑species in unpredictable arts)
rubrics_metrics.description: In unpredictable arts (e.g., many chemical cases), the general rule that a single species can antedate a genus may not apply; practice must account for predictability concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 715.03 for detailed discussion; assess whether showing one species truly establishes possession of the genus given predictability in the field.
